author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing 'human' because the bead presents two non-equivalent options without recommendation, and both touch the canonical foundation crate's public API surface (7 fields across GetResponse + SetResponse) with workspace propagation implications.

Option (a) 'change to #[serde(default)] Vec<T> / HashMap<...>': wire-shape change from 'null'/omitted to '[]'/'{}'/omitted (depending on skip_serializing_if). Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates", any reshape of jmap-types ripples through the 30-crate cookie-cutter family. Every test fixture in every server/client extension crate that uses 'Some(Vec::new())' or matches Option<Vec> would break. RFC 8620 §5.1 / §5.3 say receivers MUST treat null-as-empty, so the wire-format change is spec-conformant — but tests, fixtures, and the canonical pattern all assume the current Option<Vec> shape. This is appropriate for the 0.2.0 coordinated bump cited in the workspace root Cargo.toml lines 55-59 (the planned next coordinated workspace bump), NOT for pre-0.2 patches.

Option (b) 'add accessor helpers that auto-flatten': additive, non-breaking, but the bead itself notes it 'still leaves the pub field as the trapdoor for callers who ignore the helper'. Implementing it cleanly requires per-field iterator helpers (HashMap returning iterator-of-pairs; Vec returning iterator-of-refs) because static empty-collection sentinels are not const-constructible for HashMap.

Recommendation: defer option (a) to the planned 0.2.0 coordinated bump (alongside bd:JMAP-g7wu.1 CallerCtx, bd:JMAP-g7wu.3 helpers builder, bd:JMAP-g7wu.9 UTCDate, bd:JMAP-r3pg.14 extract_account_id). Land option (b) now if the maintainer wants the helpers as a defensive aid in 0.1.x, otherwise leave the trapdoor documented at the workspace AGENTS.md level (it's already accurately described on each field's rustdoc).

Rationale for not autonomously applying option (b):
- Adding 7 iterator helpers touches the canonical foundation crate.
- The bead's own analysis is that (b) doesn't fully solve the concern.
- The maintainer's view on 'helpers vs wire-shape-fix' may favor (a) at the next major bump.

Awaiting maintainer direction on whether to land (b) as a 0.1.x defensive aid or defer all of this to the 0.2.0 coordinated bump.
